tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy COLD-SEASON single-column run, data/eqwefic/noahcold_scm, dumped by ctessum-claude/WRF branch earthsciml-instrumented-noahcold and replayed through the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) kernels/noah_driver at ESM_DT = 60 s, WRF's OWN step. THE OUTPUTS ARE PUBLISHED, NOT DIFFERENCED. `sndens_out` and `snowh_out` are asserted against the `snp_sndens_in` and `snp_snowh_in` publishers -- the state SNOWPACK receives at entry, added on the N99 pass for the compaction component next door. That nothing modifies the density or the depth between SNOW_NEW and SNOWPACK is not an assumption: reconstructing SNOW_NEW in double precision from the dumped arguments reproduces both publishers BITWISE at all 66 pack steps of the cold set -- the 30 snowfall steps through the routine and the other 36 through SFLX's plain sneqv/snowh. So SNOW_NEW needed no instrumentation of its own; the compaction hook already carried it. WHY THE LARGEST STEP AND NOT THE SMALLEST (FORTRAN_BUGS N99, PLAN section 6). Nothing here is recovered by differencing, so there is no cancellation floor pushing the step down; and `newsn` = prcp dt 0.001 is proportional to the step, so the fresh layer's weight in the density average is too. At WRF's 60 s that weight is 1.276e-01 on this column (1.0e-3 to 1.3e-1 across the set), and at a 1e-6 s step it would be 1.7e-8 of that -- a rel 1e-9 assertion would test the snowfall physics not at all. This is the second Noah component whose reference step had to go UP rather than down, after snow compaction. ONE ASSERTION PAIR IS DIFFERENCED AND IS BOUNDED ACCORDINGLY, which puts the N99 rule inside a single test. `sndens_out` and `snowh_out` are published and hold at rel 3e-16 -- binary64 -- against their 1e-9 bound. `hnewc` and `fresh_fraction` have no publisher and must be recovered as (snp_snowh_in - snowh), a difference whose relative precision is eps divided by that same weight: 1.7e-15 here. Their bound is 1e-13, twenty times that floor, and it is a property of the REFERENCE, not of the component, which reproduces the routine bitwise. Step 26 of case A, snow falling onto initially bare frozen ground: frozen precipitation (SNOWNG); air at -8.44 C, so the fresh snow falls at density 0.07859 against a pack already at 0.07875, and the fresh layer carries 1.276e-01 of the density average.
